Tree Trimming & Pruning for Solon's Canopy Since 1982

Solon is one of Roubic's flagship markets. Thomas has worked Solon since 1982, and the mix here is unusual — heritage oaks and mature sugar and red maples in the established neighborhoods, younger canopy in the planned communities, and an east-side industrial corridor with underserved B2B commercial demand. The tree care has to fit the place.

Every prune follows ANSI A300 cuts. We never top trees and we never lion-tail mature canopy — because in Solon most jobs involve 50-to-100-year-old trees where a wrong cut compounds for decades. Oak work stays out of the April 1–July 31 window to avoid oak-wilt vector exposure, and dormant-season rotations run each February into early March.

What Happens If You Defer

The Cost of Waiting — Solon Context

Three ways a deferred prune turns a modest job into an emergency call.

Deadwood Over Structures

Left long enough, deadwood and hazard limbs over roofs, driveways, and walkways become failure points. A $375–$500 prune can turn into an emergency removal after the branch is already down.

Bad Cuts Compound

Topping and lion-tailing by other crews trigger decay and weak regrowth in Solon's mature 50-to-100-year canopy. Correcting those cuts later costs far more than doing ANSI A300 work the first time.

Missing the Oak Window

Oak work has to stay out of the April 1–July 31 vector window. Miss the dormant season and a hazardous oak limb can sit unaddressed for a full year until it's safe to cut.

Common Solon Pruning Questions

Solon Tree Trimming & Pruning FAQ

Six things Solon homeowners and property managers want to know before booking.

How much does tree pruning cost in Solon, OH?
Pruning in Solon typically runs $250–$1,500 per tree depending on size, species, and access, with larger heritage and specimen work ranging higher — $800–$1,800 for large trees and $1,800–$2,500+ for crane-assisted specimen jobs. Multi-tree dormant-rotation contracts qualify for 15–20% package savings under per-tree rates, and most dormant pruning is scheduled between February and early March.
When is the best time to prune trees in Solon, OH?
For most Solon canopy species, late winter (February through early March) is the ideal window — trees are dormant, sap flow is minimized, and pruning wounds heal cleanest heading into spring growth. The exception is oak, which we never prune between April 1 and July 31 due to oak-wilt vector exposure during sap-feeding beetle activity.
Do I need a permit to prune trees in Solon, OH?
Solon maintains a tree preservation ordinance with separate residential and commercial permit categories. Trees on public right-of-way require coordination with the city; most private-property pruning does not. Roubic assesses DBH and confirms permit requirements at the estimate, handles the coordination in-house, and bills any filing fees at cost with no markup.
What's the difference between crown reduction and crown thinning in Solon, OH?
Crown reduction shortens the overall canopy size by selectively cutting back to lateral branches — used to reduce wind exposure or clearance issues. Crown thinning removes select interior branches to reduce density without changing overall size — used to improve light penetration and reduce wind-loading. Both follow ANSI A300 cuts and never exceed 25% live-canopy removal in a single visit.
Does Roubic offer multi-tree pruning contracts in Solon, OH?
Yes. Multi-tree maintenance contracts are available across Solon on a dormant-season rotation in late winter. Most contracts qualify for 15–20% package savings under per-tree pricing and lock in the same crew year over year for canopy continuity.
Does Roubic handle commercial and corporate-campus pruning in Solon?
Yes — Solon's east-side industrial corridor and corporate campuses are a core part of our work here, including recurring seasonal pruning contracts. Commercial jobs coordinate with Solon engineering for right-of-way and sidewalk impact where needed, and we carry general liability and workers-compensation coverage with a certificate of insurance available on request.
